data.title: Canada Deems Vancouver Port Expansion a National Priority in Bid to Diversify Trade — Update
data.description:
By Paul Vieira

OTTAWA--Canada declared as a national priority a proposed expansion at the country's busiest port in Vancouver, British Columbia, arguing that it is required for the country to meet its goal of doubling non-U.S. exports by 2035.

The designation also kicks off an accelerated regulatory review process, whereby officials are tasked with determining how the expansion proceeds and under what conditions, as opposed to whether it requires approval.

Officials said this puts the timing for a final investment decision from the Vancouver Fraser Port Authority by mid-2027.

"We cannot afford to let bottlenecks hold back Canadian trade," Canadian Transport Minister Steven MacKinnon said Friday at a press conference in suburban Vancouver. "The sooner we build the [trade] capacity Canada needs, the sooner Canadian businesses and workers can benefit."

The authority, which manages the Vancouver port, said the expansion project would increase container capacity by about 50%, through a new land-mass and wharf structure covering 300 acres. This additional capacity could support annual trade of 100 billion Canadian dollars (US$71.5 billion).

Officials peg the project's cost at C$5.9 billion. Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney has pledged up to C$10 billion in financial support for Pacific coast trade corridors.

The port authority said the Vancouver terminal currently handles more than C$1 billion in commerce daily, and more cargo than the next five largest Canadian ports combined.

The expansion, upgrade and construction of trade corridors across Canada is a priority initiative for Carney, who has argued that it is necessary to restore resilience in the economy and reduce the country's reliance on U.S. trade to drive economic growth.

According to government documents, there needs to be a "significant expansion" of Canada's port capacity to diversify trade, adding that 80% of trade with non-U.S. markets is done by sea. The prime minister has set a goal of doubling the level of non-U.S. exports by 2035.

"Continued inaction on port expansion could eventually force Canadian importers and exporters to utilize U.S. ports--a dependency that is untenable in the current geopolitical circumstances," officials said, according to documents distributed at a technical briefing. "Port expansion is thus integral to ensuring Canadian sovereignty and control over key economic linkages to the rest of the world," the officials said, according to the documents.

Officials warned that without port expansion, Canada could face sharply higher shipping costs of up to C$900 million a year due to traffic congestion and insufficient capacity.

Bank of Canada researchers warned this year that the country lacked the port capacity to executive the government's trade agenda.

The central bank's analysis indicated Canadian ports can't accommodate some of the latest ultra-large container ships being deployed. Because of this, some goods originating from China and destined for Canada and loaded onto these big vessels have to dock in Los Angeles--and those goods could be subject to U.S. tariffs.

Write to Paul Vieira at paul.vieira@wsj.com

data.title: Jio Platforms Q2 results: Profit rises 14%; company eyes 340 million mobile broadband users
data.description:
Mumbai, Oct. 30 -- Jio Platforms Ltd reported a 13.7% year-on-year rise in September-quarter profit, supported by subscriber additions and growth in its broadband and digital services businesses, as the newly listed company looks to tap a larger opportunity in mobile broadband and expand beyond connectivity.

The company sees an opportunity to add 340 million mobile broadband (4G/5G) users in India over the next five years, including 240 million existing 2G users and 100 million new users, Jio Platforms chief executive Pankaj Pawar said during a post-results call with analysts. Jio also plans to expand its home broadband business, grow its enterprise offerings and build more digital services on top of its connectivity platform.

The September-quarter results are the company's first since its shares debuted on the stock exchanges on 28 October, delivering listing gains of 21.4% over the issue price of Rs.1,119. The company is now India's second-most valuable company after its parent Reliance Industries Ltd.

Jio Platforms, which houses Reliance Industries' telecom and digital services businesses, reported a 13.7% year-on-year and 8% sequential increase in net profit to Rs.8,389 crore. The company said profit growth was partly offset by higher finance costs following the capitalization of 5G assets in March, as network assets became operational.

Revenue from operations rose 11.4% year-on-year and 3.3% sequentially to Rs.40,475 crore. Jio said it delivered double-digit revenue growth across its connectivity and digital services businesses.

"This quarter's results continue to reflect the strength of our 5G network, and the growing reach of our broadband and digital services," Akash M. Ambani, managing director of Jio Platforms, said in a statement. "We would continue to build our capabilities across satellite communications, 6G intellectual property and AI embedded in our core voice and data services as we create lasting value for all our stakeholders."

In the April-June quarter, revenue from operations had risen 2.4% sequentially and 12% year-on-year to Rs.39,173 crore. Net profit stood at Rs.7,765 crore, up 9.2% from a year earlier but down 2.15% sequentially.

Jio announced its results after market hours on Friday. Its shares closed 1.1% higher at Rs.1,437.50 on the National Stock Exchange.

Earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortization (Ebitda) rose 16.6% year-on-year to Rs.21,879 crore in the September quarter, aided by revenue growth, operating leverage and margin expansion. Ebitda margin expanded 250 basis points from a year earlier to 54.1%.

Jio's average revenue per user (Arpu), a key measure of telecom operators' earnings from subscribers, rose 1.5% sequentially and 3.5% year-on-year to Rs.218.8 a month in the September quarter, from Rs.215.6 in the preceding quarter.

Promotional 5G offers continue to constrain Arpu growth, while a better subscriber mix and increased usage are contributing positively, the company said.

Tariff increases are generally seen as a key lever for telecom operators to lift Arpu. Jio continues to lag Bharti Airtel in the metric. Airtel's Arpu stood at Rs.264 in the June quarter. The company is yet to announce its September-quarter results.

In the absence of tariff hikes, Jio's sequential Arpu growth has remained largely flat over the past few quarters.

Jio's financial performance assumes significance as it begins reporting as a listed company and commands a market capitalization of about Rs.13 trillion. Globally, it is also approaching the fifth position among major telecom operators by market capitalization, despite annual revenue of Rs.1.47 trillion being lower than that of global peers.

The company's return on average capital employed stood at 11% at the end of September, compared with 12.5% a year earlier, according to its earnings release.

According to analysts, Jio's rapid expansion in wireless and home broadband has supported its valuation. Alongside this, its focus on building a technology company, with a digital services vertical backed by an integrated technology stack, offers long-term earnings visibility.

Beyond connectivity, Jio is looking to monetize its customer base through a digital gateway strategy. This involves offering services such as cloud computing, cloud gaming, video analytics and artificial intelligence-enabled features on top of basic connectivity.

The company aims to move beyond simply bundling third-party apps and instead drive customer awareness, adoption and usage of digital services, eventually converting them into additional revenue streams.

Jio also sees an opportunity to offer integrated connectivity, cloud, computing and security solutions to India's estimated 80 million small merchants, many of which lack dedicated technology teams, Pawar said.

International expansion is another focus area, although the company intends to take a selective, asset-light approach rather than make large investments in overseas telecom infrastructure.

"We will be very, very selective about the international markets that we will go to," Ambani told analysts, adding that Jio would operate as a managed services partner, leveraging its proprietary technology stack instead of making capital-intensive investments in towers and fibre infrastructure.

Jio's telecom business, operated through Reliance Jio Infocomm Ltd, accounts for about 88% of Jio Platforms' revenue.

Reliance Jio added 9.1 million subscribers in the September quarter, taking its total subscriber base to 542.4 million. It had added 8.9 million subscribers in the preceding quarter.

Its 5G subscriber base reached 300 million at the end of September, an increase of 66 million over the past 12 months, making it the world's largest 5G operator outside China, the company said.

Jio's fixed broadband subscriber base stood at 30 million, with 7.3 million additions over the past 12 months. Jio AirFiber, with a subscriber base of 15.1 million, accounted for more than 75% of the company's fixed broadband additions during the period, it said.

Pawar said Jio sees the potential to expand its home broadband footprint to 150 million households by FY31.

"We believe this is the great opportunity for Jio to keep continuing particularly when we don't need any incremental spectrum and when we don't need any incremental capex to be deployed to take our balanced 4G base into 5G," Pawar said.

data.title: RIL, JPL Q2 results 2026 impact: Reliance Industries, Jio Platforms shares in focus on Monday 2 Nov - What to expect?
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 30 -- Reliance Industries and Jio Platforms are set to be in the spotlight on Monday after announcing their Q2 FY27 results, with investors assessing the earnings impact on both stocks.

The results mark an important milestone for recently listed Jio Platforms, which has become the second-largest listed entity in the Reliance Group by market capitalisation, after Reliance Industries

The market reaction on Monday will offer the first indication of how investors are evaluating the two companies' latest quarterly performance.

Reliance Industries Ltd reported a record consolidated profit after tax (PAT) of Rs.29,550 crore for the July-September quarter (Q2 FY27), marking a 33.8% increase from Rs.22,092 crore in the year-ago period. Revenue rose 27.8% year-on-year (YoY) to Rs.3,62,268 crore, while EBITDA increased 23.9% to a record Rs.62,409 crore.

The strong performance was primarily driven by a recovery in the oil-to-chemicals (O2C) business, where EBITDA surged 67.9% to Rs.25,203 crore, supported by higher global fuel margins and improved petrochemical spreads. O2C revenue increased 44.2% to Rs.2,31,601 crore, with supply disruptions in West Asia and other regions pushing transportation fuel cracks higher.

Digital services also supported earnings, while the retail business remained a relative weak spot. Reliance Retail Ventures reported a 24.3% decline in PAT to Rs.2,611 crore, despite a 6.4% rise in revenue to Rs.91,716 crore. Its EBITDA, before a one-time impairment charge, fell 8.6% to Rs.6,228 crore.

Commenting on the results, Chairman Mukesh Ambani said the company's businesses delivered a strong performance despite volatile commodity markets and geopolitical tensions. He highlighted the particularly strong performance of the O2C business, supported by tight fuel markets, improved downstream petrochemical margins and firm domestic demand.

Jio Platforms reported an 11.3% YoY increase in revenue to Rs.47,485 crore for Q2 FY27, while EBITDA rose 16.6% to Rs.21,879 crore. Its EBITDA margin expanded 250 basis points to 54.1%, while profit after tax increased 13.7% to Rs.8,387 crore.

The company's average revenue per user (ARPU) rose to Rs.218.8 per month from Rs.211.4 a year earlier. Its subscriber base reached 542.4 million, including 300 million 5G users, while fixed broadband connections crossed 30 million homes.

The quarterly results come three days after Jio Platforms completed its Rs.30,188-crore initial public offering (IPO). The shares made a strong market debut at a 26.7% premium to the issue price, taking the company's market capitalisation to around Rs.13.1 lakh crore and making it the second-most valuable listed company in the Reliance Group after Reliance Industries.

Chairman Mukesh Ambani described Jio's listing as a historic moment in Reliance's value-creation journey, highlighting the strong investor response to the IPO, which was subscribed more than 22 times.

data.title: How This Under-the-Radar Quantum Stock Could More Than Double — Barrons.com
data.description:
By Mackenzie Tatananni

Investors looking for cheap exposure to quantum computing may have a new entry point. Freshly public Pasqal is already building systems and landing high-profile partnerships — and one analyst sees the stock doubling.

Though well regarded at home, the French quantum developer is still finding its footing in U.S. markets. Pasqal's blank-check merger in August was part of a broader wave that carried several emerging players onto public exchanges, but building name recognition remains an ongoing effort.

The stock received a welcome Wall Street endorsement on Friday as Cantor Fitzgerald analyst Troy Jensen — who previously discussed his quantum stock picks in an interview with Barron's — launched coverage at Overweight with a $12 target.

Jensen's target suggests shares could rise over 134% from current levels. Pasqal slipped 2.3% to $5.12 on Friday, in line with an extensive slump in tech stocks.

While broader commercialization of quantum technology is years away in the most optimistic scenario, Pasqal is laying out a clear go-to-market strategy, Jensen argued. The company focuses on a handful of "key verticals" including energy, financial services, and specialty materials.

This narrow scope was on display in September, when Pasqal unveiled a partnership with USA Rare Earth to develop better separation chemicals in a step toward making mineral processing plants smaller, cheaper, and more energy-efficient.

Pasqal's key differentiator is its approach to quantum computing: neutral atoms. Alongside Infleqtion, it is one of just two publicly traded companies using this architecture, which suspends individual atoms inside a vacuum chamber and manipulates them with lasers.

Every modality comes with trade-offs. Neutral atoms are generally slower than superconducting qubits, the more mature approach backed by industry heavyweights like IBM. Yet what neutral-atom systems surrender in speed, they gain in scalability and coherence times, theoretically allowing them to run more complex programs.

The underlying science matters more to researchers than to enterprise customers, who only look for the performance and accuracy to validate their investment.

Pasqal approaches this challenge by combining analog and digital processing. The analog mode excels at simulating raw quantum phenomena for specific tasks, whereas gate-based digital systems deliver the flexibility required for structured, algorithmic logic.

This dual approach "offers the opportunity for near-term value" while error-corrected systems mature, Jensen argued. Because digital quantum setups accumulate errors rapidly as they scale, Pasqal's hardware lets organizations deploy systems today for practical analog applications, then transition their existing stack to fault-tolerant digital logic as the technology evolves.

Jensen expects revenue growth to accelerate over the next few years as timelines for higher-performance systems coalesce toward the end of the decade. For investors willing to stomach near-term volatility, Pasqal offers a front-row seat to that transition as it pushes neutral atoms into the mainstream.

data.title: US to return to standard time Sunday as lawmakers rebuff Trump push
data.description:
By David Shepardson

President Donald Trump's months-long push to prod lawmakers to end the twice yearly practice of changing the clocks — including posting the phone number of a US senator this month — has run out of time this year.

The United States will return to standard time on Sunday at 2 a.m. ET and it will continue until March 14, despite Trump's repeated efforts to convince the Senate to follow the US House and make daylight saving time permanent year round.

Earlier this month, Trump shared the phone number of Republican Senator Tom Cotton, who has been a strong critic of making daylight saving time permanent, in a push to get him to support the bill. He called dozens of other senators seeking their support.

"The United States Senate is letting the Daylight Saving Time bill die," Trump wrote this week on social media, again urging action.

The US House of Representatives in July ​voted 308-117 to end the twice-yearly practice of changing clocks ​observed across most of the nation since the 1960s.

Earlier this month, Senate Majority Leader John Thune told Politico there is no consensus and "no clear path forward." Congressional aides say there is likely not enough time remaining to take up the issue when the Senate returns for a brief post-election session.

Critics note the change would mean the sun rises an hour later on winter mornings, leaving more children traveling to school and commuters, construction workers, farmers and others heading to work before daylight. In some places, the sun ​would not rise until ​nearly 9 a.m. or ⁠later at the height of winter.

Supporters say changing the clocks disrupts sleep, increases workplace injuries and contributes to more road accidents. They argue keeping ​clocks an hour ahead year-round would provide more evening daylight and boost ​economic activity ⁠during the winter months.

If enacted, clocks would no longer return to standard time in 2027, although states could opt out of year-round daylight saving time if they do not currently observe it or voted ⁠to adopt ​permanent standard time before the law was changed.

The US ​used year-round daylight saving time during World War Two and enacted it again in 1974 to reduce energy use. But ​it proved deeply unpopular and Congress repealed it later that year.

data.title: Fed officials make case for rate hikes amid ongoing inflation concerns
data.description:
Key points:
  • Trio of Fed officials argued for rate hikes in comments Friday
  • Officials argued for action to ensure inflation returns to target
  • Rate hike calls first after steady policy meeting earlier in week

By Ann Saphir and Michael S. Derby

A trio of Federal Reserve officials made the case on Friday for more interest rate increases to combat high levels of inflation, in the first round of commentary made by central bankers after this week’s monetary policy meeting that saw short-term borrowing costs left steady.

Calling the current level of price pressures and the time inflation has been above the 2% “unacceptable,” Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas President Lorie Logan said the central bank has more work to do.

“It remains clear to me, given the current outlook, that the (Federal Open Market Committee) needs to implement at least two more 25-basis-point rate increases,” Logan said in the text of a speech prepared for an event at Davidson College.

After delivering those increases, “it would make sense in my view to pause and examine economic and financial developments to determine what further action may be appropriate,” Logan said.

Logan holds a voting role on the FOMC this year and joined with her colleagues in favor of the FOMC’s decision to hold its interest rate target range steady at between 3.75% and 4%. Logan explained that not moving the target at the meeting held over Tuesday and Wednesday came amid volatile markets and gave the public time to adjust to the shift toward higher borrowing costs.

Speaking separately, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis President Alberto Musalem, who does not hold a vote on the FOMC this year, also argued for higher rates.

"Additional firming of monetary policy will be necessary, and soon," Musalem said in the text of a speech to be presented at an event held by the Shadow Open Market Committee, a group that takes stock of Fed actions and policies.

"Incremental adjustments made earlier are usually less disruptive than larger and abrupt actions taken later," he said.

Musalem said that inflation remains too high relative to the 2% target and added that it was unlikely to ease absent Fed action. He noted that monetary policy is not in a position to lower inflation at the current moment.

"I believe that monetary policy and financial conditions remain accommodative. Financial conditions tightened recently," Musalem said.

Meanwhile, Richmond Fed leader Thomas Barkin said in an interview on SiriusXM's Business Briefing that “inflation's high, demand is solid, unemployment is relatively low. So I think the direction of travel is pretty straightforward” for future interest rate increases.

“The question, though, is pace ... We ​signaled a gradual approach. Gradual makes sense when you're not much behind the ⁠curve, where you want time to learn,” Barkin said.

MORE WORK TO DO

The officials spoke on Friday as the central bank’s so-called blackout period that limits communications around FOMC meetings ended.

Two Fed officials dissented at the gathering but in a break from what has become a common process, neither Cleveland Fed leader Beth Hammack nor Fed Governor Lisa Cook offered formal explanation Friday for why they voted in favor of a rate hike.

The Fed raised rates in September to help bring persistently high inflation pressures back to the 2% target and officials have broadly signaled they are not done, with traders and investors eyeing the December meeting as the next time to act.

After the FOMC meeting, Chairman Kevin Warsh was asked at a press conference why the Fed didn’t hike rates at this week’s gathering if it thinks inflation is too high.

“I'm encouraged by the progress we've made in a short period of time” on lowering inflation, Warsh said, “but if the crux of your question is, you haven't delivered yet, you haven't achieved price stability, you're right about that. But we're working on it.”

The Fed leader, who has been loath to provide guidance about the interest rate outlook, did not say what he thought the Fed would do at the Dec. 8-9 policy meeting.

Futures markets have been easing back on expectations of a December rate hike though market participants still believe an increase in short-term borrowing costs is more likely than holding steady.

Stock indexes were suffering large declines on Friday, with the Nasdaq falling to its weakest level in three months, as artificial intelligence developments rattled investors.

Adding to the uncertainty of the outlook is next Tuesday’s midterm elections in the US, which could see major advances by Democratic candidates, driven by voters who’ve shown deep discontent over inflation and the impact of President Donald Trump’s Middle East war.

The market’s worry that AI-related activity might slow could take some pressure off the Fed if realized. That's because central bankers have for some time noted that very hot levels of technology investment have helped drive up inflation. Slower activity in that sector might help ease price pressures and reduce the need for the Fed to raise rates.

(TheNewswire)

    Toronto, Ontario – TheNewswire - October 30, 2026 – Ventripoint Diagnostics Ltd. (“Ventripoint” or the “Corporation”, TSXV:VPT) announces that it will seek approval of TSX Venture Exchange (“TSXV” or the “Exchange”) to extend its previously announced non-brokered private placement (“Offering”) of up to 3,500,000 units (each, a “Unit”) at a price of $0.10 per Unit. data.title: Wall Street closes sharply lower as AI cash burn fears spark tech selloff
data.description:
Key points:
  • Nasdaq posts largest one-day percentage drop since early June
  • Intel slides after reporting big cash burn
  • Crypto firms slide after reports that hackers stole $6.3 billion from Binance

By Stephen Culp and Purvi Agarwal

US stocks tumbled on Friday, with the Nasdaq suffering its largest one-day percentage drop since June 5 following disappointing quarterly results from Intel and Amazon, which amplified growing worries surrounding AI-related companies' massive spending on the nascent technology.

All three major US stock indexes slumped, with the tech-heavy Nasdaq suffering the steepest loss.

The tech rout was sparked by disappointing quarterly results from Intel and Amazon released late on Thursday.

Chip stocks veered sharply lower, dragging the Philadelphia SE Semiconductor Index to a monthly loss.

"It's fair to say that this week, not just today, has been very much about the future of AI and what that's going to look like, whether there will be a positive return on investment and if so, how quickly," said Oliver Pursche, senior vice president at Wealthspire Advisors in New York.

"Companies that are performing and meeting the very lofty expectations that have been set are doing well," Pursche added. "Those that are falling short and seem to be missing the mark or not executing as expected are getting punished."

All three main equity indexes closed lower on the week. The S&P 500 and the Nasdaq logged monthly losses, while the Dow exited October with a gain.

According to preliminary data, the S&P 500 CBOE:SPX lost 139.30 points, or 1.80%, to end at 7,580.21 points, while the Nasdaq Composite lost 747.73 points, or 2.84%, to 25,440.68. The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 571.98 points, or 1.09%, to 51,770.58.

Third-quarter earnings season has passed the halfway mark, with 299 companies in the S&P 500 having reported. Of those, 82% have beaten consensus expectations, according to LSEG data.

Analysts now expect third-quarter S&P 500 earnings growth of 31.6%, year-on-year, per LSEG.

Oil supermajors Exxon Mobil and Chevron both beat quarterly profit expectations, benefiting from soaring profit margins as a result of energy supply disruptions arising from the US-Israeli war with Iran and Russia's war in Ukraine.

Starbucks dipped after the coffee chain forecast an annual revenue decline due to its divestiture of its Chinese business.

Cryptocurrency-related firms Coinbase , Strategy , and Robinhood fell in the wake of reports that hackers stole $6.3 billion from Binance, the world's biggest cryptocurrency exchange.

data.title: Grains Futures End Month With a Whimper — Daily Grain Highlights
data.description:
By Anthony Harrup

  • Corn for December delivery fell 0.8% Friday on the Chicago Board of Trade to $4.47 3/4 a bushel, trading around the $4.50 level as the market continues to look for more demand signals.
  • Soybeans for January delivery settled little changed at $12.34 1/4 a bushel.
  • Wheat for December delivery ended near flat at $6.03 1/4 a bushel.

The Right Price: Grains traders are focused on finding a price level that will stimulate demand and help rally the markets, said Brian Hoops of Midwest Market Solutions.

Wheat in particular tried to rally on news that China had inquired about U.S. wheat, "but an inquiry and a purchase are different things and no purchases have been announced," he said. If China does buy wheat, it should lift both wheat and corn "as it would be an indication that demand will improve at current price levels."

Flash Sales: The USDA reported two new flash sales of soybeans for the 2026-27 marketing year, one for 165,150 metric tons and another for 132,000 tons, both to unknown destinations.

Soybean export sales have had a strong start to the 2026-27 marketing year, but "strong harvest reports and a good start to the South American growing season have kept managed funds in liquidation mode," Doug Bergman of RCM Alternatives said in a note.

INSIGHT

Rain Delay: The soybean and corn harvests could be interrupted as more rain is expected this weekend and early next week across much of the Midwest, Mike Castle of StoneX said in a note.

Systems are already moving across much of Texas/Oklahoma and northern Missouri into Iowa/Illinois, "likely knocking combines back out of the field and slowing the tail-end of harvest," he said. "It will be interesting to keep an eye on the impact seen in the cash markets given the combination of delayed harvest and sharply lower prices reducing farmers' incentive to sell across the scale."

Weather Watch: It is difficult to be bearish corn under $4.50 a bushel, wheat under $6 and soybeans under $12.30 unless favorable Brazilian weather is confirmed in November-December, AgResource said in a note. Brazilian forecasts will be in focus starting next week, and while there are no problems with Argentine soil moisture or pace of corn and soy planting, there is a significant risk of a lingering El Niño negatively affecting rainfall in key soybean producing regions of Brazil, the firm added.

AHEAD

  • The USDA is scheduled to release its weekly Grain Export Inspections Report at 11 a.m. EST Monday.
  • The USDA is due to release its monthly Grain Crushings Report at 3 p.m. EST Monday.
  • The USDA is scheduled to release its monthly Oilseed Crushings Report at 3 p.m. EST Monday.
  • The USDA is due to release its weekly Crop Progress Report at 4 p.m. EST Monday.
  • Archer-Daniels Midland Co. is scheduled to announce its 3Q earnings before the stock market opens Tuesday.

A barred former LPL Financial investment advisor and broker has pleaded guilty to wire fraud in connection with a scheme that prosecutors say cost three financial services companies more than $3.3 million. Andrew Komarow, 37, of Avon, Conn., had initially pleaded not guilty to 11 charges but entered a guilty plea to a lone count in federal court last week. Prosecutors say that Andrew Komarow made a series of unfunded electronic transfers and attempted to recoup the money through high-risk options trading.

Among other most-read articles:

Clients should have a variety of retirement accounts. Most investors understand the need for diversification across U.S. stocks, international stocks, and bonds, but fewer recognize the value of diversifying allocations among savings vehicles. A mix of IRAs, Roth IRAs, and investment accounts can offer retirees tax-efficient options when they need cash. Our guest columnist writes that he has seen people reach their 60s with nearly all of their nest egg in an account, such as a traditional IRA, where distributions are taxable.

J,P. Morgan raises its long-term 60/40 forecast. The long-term outlook for investors is improving, according to J.P. Morgan Asset Management, which recently published its annual report detailing long-term capital market assumptions. The firm now projects annual returns of 7% on traditional 60/40 stock/bond portfolios over the next 10 to 15 years, an increase of 0.6 percentage point from the 6.4% return rate forecast a year ago.

Wealthy clients are buying businesses for their kids. Some wealthy entrepreneurs are taking a different approach to inheritance. Instead of leaving their adult children large nest eggs, they are buying businesses and then involving their children in running them. For older entrepreneurs who aren't quite ready to retire, buying and growing a business with their children becomes part hobby and part training ground for the next generation.

LPL Financial shares plunged nearly 15% on Wednesday after its third-quarter results revealed diminished expectations for its acquisition of Commonwealth Financial Network. The financial services company beat Wall Street's estimates for its earnings but said it now expects to retain about 83% of the assets that Commonwealth advisors oversaw. data.title: CBOT wheat closes lower, sets ninth straight weekly loss
data.description:
Chicago Board of Trade wheat futures edged lower on Friday and set a ninth consecutive weekly loss, as prices remained pressured by prospects of increased Russian wheat exports, and despite strong demand for US grain and reports that China could buy from the United States, market analysts said.

  • CBOT December soft red winter wheat (WZ26) settled down 1/4 cent at $6.03-1/2 per bushel.

  • The most-active contract on a continuous basis ended down more than 3% for the week, and has fallen more than 23% over the past nine weeks.

  • K.C. December hard red winter wheat (KWZ26) ended down 1 cent at $6.44-1/4 a bushel and Minneapolis December spring wheat (MWEZ26) fell 3/4 cent at $6.23-3/4 a bushel.

  • Shipments from the Black Sea could increase after sources said Russia, the world's largest wheat exporter, had allowed grain export vessels to leave the Sea of Azov for the first time since July 10.

  • However, attacks continue in the region, with a Greek container ship sunk on Thursday. On the demand side, Bloomberg reported on Thursday that buyers in China, the world's biggest crop importer, were seeking offers on US soft red winter wheat.

  • Traders have also been keeping a close eye on both geopolitical stress and investor positioning ahead of next week's US election, said market analysts.

  • And managed funds hold a sizable net short position in CBOT wheat futures, leaving the market primed for a short-covering bounce.

data.title: Billions of Dollars In Cryptocurrency Was Just Stolen. Should Investors Be Worried? — Barrons.com
data.description:
By Joe Light

A massive crypto hack just gave investors a reminder that the industry still hasn't solved the cybersecurity issues that have plagued it since its inception.

But that likely won't slow Wall Street's embrace of crypto and the technology that underpins it.

Crypto exchange Binance said Thursday it had been hit by hackers who stole more than $6.3 billion worth of Bitcoin, Ethereum, and stablecoins such as USDC and Tether, among other tokens. Blockchain securities researchers including Chainalysis identified a North Korea-based hacking group as the likely perpetrator. Binance in statements on X said it would cover any losses with its own funds and that "user funds are safe."

Details of how the hack was pulled off are still emerging, but the attack highlighted why crypto has long been such an alluring target.

Traditional ways of moving money and other assets often take days, involve intermediaries, and have ways of stopping or even reversing transfers. But Bitcoin and other cryptocurrencies can transfer almost instantly — and irreversibly — and can be quickly laundered among thousands of wallet addresses to hide where the funds have gone.

The Binance hack doesn't appear to have a direct impact on the major spot Bitcoin exchange-traded funds, which use Coinbase Global or other firms as their custodians. The largest such funds include BlackRock's iShares Bitcoin Trust, the Fidelity Wise Origin Bitcoin Fund, and the Grayscale Bitcoin Trust.

Each of those funds in documents says their Bitcoin custodian keeps a substantial portion of the cryptocurrency offline in so-called "cold" wallets, protecting against a hacker gaining access. A smaller amount of Bitcoin is still typically kept in hot wallets to allow for the creation and redemption of shares.

Still, if a hacker somehow did gain access to the Bitcoin in these funds, their prospectuses make clear that the investors could experience a loss. The iShares prospectus, for example, notes that the Bitcoin isn't protected by the insurance that typically protects securities and deposits from theft. While its custodian, Coinbase, does have an insurance policy that could cover some losses, it isn't enough to cover the whole fund. Fidelity's and Grayscale's prospectuses have similar disclosures.

The risk isn't entirely theoretical. The Federal Bureau of Investigation in 2024 put out an alert warning that North Korean cyber actors "conducted research on a variety of targets connected to cryptocurrency exchange-traded funds (ETFs) over the last several months."

Grayscale, in a statement Friday, said its products and customers were unaffected by the Binance hack and that "safeguarding digital assets is the foundation of how we serve investors."

Coinbase didn't respond to a request for comment. The company wasn't hit by the hack and on social media said it was reaching out to Binance to offer help and was blocking compromised crypto wallets from sending the currencies.

"Crypto has been through many tough times, and has always come out stronger on the other side. This won't be any different," said Coinbase CEO Brian Armstrong in a post on X.

President Donald Trump's administration has been one of the biggest boosters of U.S. crypto adoption, and on Friday, there was little indication that would change.

Commodity Futures Trading Commission Chairman Michael Selig in a CNBC interview said that the theft of crypto rather than, say, cash from a bank would make it easier for law enforcement to track the stolen funds.

Crypto proponents could use the theft as an argument to push for a revival of legislation like the Clarity Act, an industry-supported bill that would have taken most crypto trading out of the purview of securities regulators, said Mark Hays, an associate director at investor protection group Americans for Financial Reform and Demand Progress.

"They'll say 'Yes, this is awful, but this is why we wanted a more robust regulatory framework in the first place,'" Hays said. "The truth is it's not clear any of the proposals would have prevented this from happening."

As to the hack's effect on crypto prices or on Wall Street's headlong adoption of blockchain technology for stocks and other traditional assets, good history lessons can be found in what happened after previous major hacks, said Clear Street analyst Owen Lau.

Crypto exchange Mt. Gox collapsed in 2014 after losing more than $350 million in Bitcoin to theft. The loss of confidence damaged prices and trading volumes for a while, but Bitcoin prices soon went on to new heights, Lau noted.

Similarly, Wall Street firms that are on the path to "tokenizing" traditional assets aren't likely to give up those plans because of the Binance hack, Lau said.

Traditional Wall Street firms in the past year have announced or rolled out projects that would "tokenize" stocks and other securities, allowing them trade over blockchains in a similar fashion to Bitcoin and other cryptocurrencies. The idea is to allow them to transfer and settle almost instantly 24/7 rather than over the full business day it takes now.

In some cases, those efforts include blockchains that are only open to approved, institutional participants.

"The conversation with the senior level [of a firm] will get much more difficult," Lau said. "But I don't think it will slow them down in any sense."

Write to Joe Light at joe.light@barrons.com

data.title: Mergers and acquisitions
data.description:
The following bids, mergers, acquisitions and disposals were reported by 2000 GMT on Friday:

** US private equity CD&R is exploring a deal to take payments processor Global Payments private, according to a source familiar with the deal.

** Valero Energy said its unit, Valero Refining-Texas, agreed to acquire the former Houston refinery site owned by a subsidiary of LyondellBasell Industries for $320.5 million.

** German chemicals group Evonik said that BASF's sweetened takeover offer was not enough to persuade it to start formal deal talks, but it has asked the suitor's management to elaborate on the rationale for its bid.

** Spanish transport company Autobuses de Leon made an offer to buy Mobico Group in a deal that would value the British bus, coach and rail services company at about £308 million ($412 million) on a fully diluted basis.

** Tesco, Britain's largest supermarket chain , said it will sell its businesses in the Czech Republic and Slovakia to Dutch retailer Ahold Delhaize for an enterprise value of €1.7 billion ($1.90 billion), marking the latest step in its long retreat from overseas markets.

** Asia-focused investment firm PAG will acquire a 51% stake in Evergrande Property Services Group , a unit of debt-laden developer China Evergrande Group, for HK$4.03 billion ($514 million), the two said in a joint announcement.

** Czech billionaire Michal Strnad has offered €30 billion to acquire Delfin, the investment vehicle of Italy's Del Vecchio family and the key shareholder in eyewear giant EssilorLuxottica , two people close to the matter told Reuters.

** Business software maker Salesforce said on Thursday it would buy defense technology company Rune Technologies to expand its Missionforce business, which serves the US military and government agencies.

** Perrigo said on Thursday that it will sell its infant formula business to privately held contract manufacturing firm MeridianMade for up to $175 million, as the consumer health products company sharpens its focus on over-the-counter medicines and self-care products.

** The Canadian government is taking an equity stake in Cohere, joining a funding round led by Germany's Schwarz Group targeting C$7 billion ($4.49 billion) for the Toronto-based AI lab, Cohere said on Thursday.

** Residential security firm ADT has agreed to be taken private for $7.6 billion by Thrive Holdings, a permanent capital vehicle created by Josh Kushner's Thrive Capital to buy businesses in critical industries and improve their prospects with technology, including AI.

** DoorDash said on Thursday it would buy Instacart in a deal valued at about $17 billion, stepping up its push into the fast-growing US grocery delivery market as competition intensifies among app-based platforms.

** Banca Monte dei Paschi's shareholders on Thursday rejected, with 90.9% of votes, CEO Luigi Lovaglio's proposal for an exchange offer to buy wealth manager Banca Generali .
